'''Enrique Omar Sívori''' ({{IPA|es|enˈrike oˈmaɾ ˈsiβoɾi|lang}}, {{IPA|it|ˈɔːmar ˈsiːvori|lang}}; 2 October 1935 – 17 February 2005) was an Argentine-Italian [[Association football|football]] player and manager who played as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. At club level, he is known for his successful time with Italian side [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] during the late 1950s and early 1960s, where he won three [[Serie A]] titles among other trophies; he also played for [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] in Argentina and [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] in Italy.

He made his international debut for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], winning the [[Copa América|South American Championship]] in [[1957 South American Championship|1957]]. Later in his career, he represented [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and took part in the [[1962 FIFA World Cup|1962 World Cup]]. After his retirement as player, he coached several teams in Argentina.

Sívori is considered as one of the best players of his generation and also one of the greatest players of all time, he was known for his skill, speed, goalscoring, technique, creativity, and his footballing talent was widely acclaimed. He won the ''[[Copa América|South American Championship]] Best Player'' award in [[1957 South American Championship|1957]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sachampfulltrivia.html|title = The Copa América Archive – Trivia}}</ref> and the coveted [[Ballon d'Or]] award in [[1961 Ballon d'Or|1961]]. He scored 432 goals in his career, including friendlies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://docs.ufpr.br/~mmsabino/sstatistics/sivori.html|title=Sívori}}</ref>

==Club career==

===River Plate===

Sívori was born in [[San Nicolás de los Arroyos]], [[Buenos Aires Province]], into a family of [[Italian Argentines|Italian]] descent. His paternal grandfather, Giulio Sivori, was an immigrant from Cavi di Lavagna, a hamlet in the [[province of Genoa]], while his mother Carolina was of [[Abruzzo|Abruzzese]] ancestry.<ref name="storiedicalcio">{{cite web|url=http://storiedicalcio.altervista.org/blog/sivori.html|title=SIVORI Omar: genio e follia dell'angelo ribelle|date=7 February 2016|publisher=Storie di Calcio|language=it|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.tuttocalciatori.net/notizie/2011/10/i-miti-del-calcio-omar-sivori/| title= I miti del calcio: Omar Sivori| date= 25 October 2011 | access-date= 5 January 2013 | work = www.tuttocalciatori.net }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/2001/02/09/sivori-la-rabbia-delloriundo-che-mafia-si.html| title= Sivori, la rabbia dell'oriundo Che mafia, si sospetta di tutti: il calcio rischia di morire| date= 9 February 2001 | access-date= 5 January 2013 | work = repubblica.it }}</ref> As a youngster Sívori became heavily interested in the game of [[association football|football]] and by the time he reached his teens he was signed up to a side from the city of [[Buenos Aires]], [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]].<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref>{{in lang|es}} [http://www.redargentina.com/DeportesArgentinos/Sivori.asp RedArgentina.com] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030922142909/http://www.redargentina.com/DeportesArgentinos/Sivori.asp |date=22 September 2003 }}</ref> The teenage Sívori was given a chance to break through into a squad which included players like the famed forward [[Ángel Labruna]] and [[Félix Loustau]] who established themselves in the era of ''[[La Máquina]]'', one of the foremost formations in football history.<ref name="RSSSF.com">{{in lang|es}} [https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/arghist-pro1950s.html rsssf.org]</ref> He soon earned the nickname ''El Cabezón'' (bighead) from the fans, due to his hair, outspokenness, confidence, arrogance, and playing style.<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="RSSSF.com"/><ref name="telegraph-sivori-obituary">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1483849/Omar-Sivori.html|title=Omar Sivori|publisher=The Telegraph|date=19 February 2005|access-date=2 October 2017}}</ref>

River was able to win the [[Argentine Primera División]] in 1955, the title was confirmed when River beat local archrival [[Boca Juniors]] 2–1 at [[Estadio Alberto J. Armando|La Bombonera]], in [[Buenos Aires]], with just one game remaining.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/arg55.html |title=Argentina 1955 |website=[[RSSSF]] |date=23 April 2009}}</ref> The same season River won the Copa Río de La Plata by beating [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] from Uruguay. The following season he had similar success when River won the Argentine league title on the final day of the season; beating [[Rosario Central]] 4–0, with Sívori scoring the final goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/arg56.html |title=Argentina 1956 |website=[[RSSSF]] |date=28 February 2008}}</ref> Sívori would play his final game for River against the same team on 5 May 1957.
[[File:Sivori river vs huracan.jpg|thumb|upright=1.13|Sívori dribbing in a match v. [[Club Atlético Huracán|Huracán]]]]

During the [[1957–58 Serie A|1957–58]] season, the 21-year-old Sívori was signed by Italian club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] after being spotted by [[Renato Cesarini]]. Juventus paid 10 million [[Argentine peso|pesos]] (the equivalent of £91,000) for the transfer, which was a [[World football transfer record|world-record transfer fee]] for the time. Sívori's move would prove bad for River's league fortunes, in the 18 years after 1957 they were unable to win the league in Argentina.<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="bbc">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_football/4283015.stm|publisher=BBC|title=Argentina mourns lost son Sivori|date=29 June 2007|first=Tim|last=Vickery}}</ref> However, they were able to complete their'' [[Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti|El Monumental]]'' stadium (previously nicknamed "the [[horseshoe]]") by adding a fourth stand bearing his name, with the money from the deal.<ref name="bbc"/>

===Juventus===
The same season two other prominent Argentines moved to the Italian league: [[Antonio Valentín Angelillo]] ([[Internazionale Milano F.C.|Inter]]) and [[Humberto Maschio]] ([[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]]). The three had all been part of [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]]'s defenders that brought home gold from the [[1957 South American Championship]]. With an emphasis on the forward line positions, the team was nicknamed ''The Angels with Dirty Faces'', a reference to cinema's then-celebrated ''[[Angels with Dirty Faces]]''–the team's irreverent style of play and lackadaisical attitude to training.<ref>{{cite book |last= Wilson |first= Jonathan|title= Angels With Dirty Faces: The Footballing History of Argentina |year= 2001 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=ia6nAwAAQBAJ&pg=PT13 |location= Hachette UK |isbn= 9781409144441}}</ref> The nickname followed the trio after the tournament and their move to Italy. In Italy, the trio were nicknamed ''The Trio of Death'', the trio's clinical ability in scoring goals.<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.maltatoday.com.mt/2005/02/27/tony.html |title=Malta Today |publisher=Malta Today |date=27 February 2005 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100101205943/http://www.maltatoday.com.mt/2005/02/27/tony.html |archive-date=1 January 2010 }}</ref>
[[File:Coppa Italia 1958-59 - Inter Milan v Juventus FC - Nicolè, Bicicli, Angelillo, Firmani, Sívori, Charles.jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.13|Sívori (right) with Juventus in 1958, while leaving the field of [[San Siro]] near his compatriot [[Antonio Valentín Angelillo|Angelillo]] of Inter Milan]]

Prior to the arrival of Sívori and Welshman [[John Charles]], Juventus had been going through somewhat of a slump. However, the duo along with experienced ''Juventino'' [[Giampiero Boniperti]] put together a formidable force and won Serie A during the 1957–58 season. Their good form continued and Sívori won two more ''scudetti'' (1959–60 and 1960–61) as well as two [[Coppa Italia]] titles (1958–59 and 1959–60), and the [[Coppa delle Alpi]] (1963). Omar Sívori's hard work had paid off and he was named [[European Footballer of the Year]] (also known as ''Ballon d'Or'') in [[1961 Ballon d'Or|1961]].<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="tuttojuve1"/><ref name="tuttosport">{{cite web|url=http://www.tuttosport.com/news/calcio/serie-a/juventus/2016/02/17-8573327/la_juventus_ricorda_sutwitter_il_mito_omar_sivori/|title=La Juventus ricorda su Twitter il mito Omar Sivori|publisher=Tutto Sport|language=it|date=17 February 2016|access-date=1 March 2017|archive-date=2 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302033150/http://www.tuttosport.com/news/calcio/serie-a/juventus/2016/02/17-8573327/la_juventus_ricorda_sutwitter_il_mito_omar_sivori/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The same year as his personal achievement however, the ''Magical Trio'' as they were known, had broken up with Boniperti's retirement and the following season John Charles moved back to [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. Sívori stayed on with the ''Old Lady'', notably scoring the only goal in a 1–0 victory against [[Real Madrid]], making Juventus the first Italian side ever to win at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]]. Sívori wore the [[Squad number (association football)|number 10 shirt]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/da-ferrari-a-bernardeschi-la-juve-e-l-importanza-della-maglia-numero-10-998150|title=Da Ferrari a Bernardeschi: la Juve e l'importanza della maglia numero 10|publisher=www.TuttoMercatoWeb.com|language=it|author1=Lorenzo Di Benedetto|date=24 July 2017|access-date=24 July 2017}}</ref> and was appointed the team's [[Captain (association football)|captain]] in 1963, but did not win any more championships or trophies with Juventus, and left after the [[1964–65 Serie A|1964–65 season]], because of a disagreement with new coach [[Heriberto Herrera]].<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="tuttojuve1"/><ref>[http://www.liminaedizioni.it/griglia_libro.cfm?art_codice=2&codice_collana=10 LiminaeDizioni.it] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070311033725/http://www.liminaedizioni.it/griglia_libro.cfm?art_codice=2&codice_collana=10 |date=11 March 2007 }}</ref>
[[File:1950s–60s Juventus FC - Omar Sívori.jpg|thumb|upright=1.13|Sívori posing in ''Bianconeri'' colours inside the [[Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino|Communal Stadium]] in Turin]]

With Juventus, Sívori scored 167 goals in 253 appearances in all competitions,<ref name="omar sivori"/> making him the club's [[Juventus F.C. statistics and records#All-time top 10 goalscorers|fifth highest goalscorer ever]] as of 2011. He also holds the [[Football records in Italy#Goalscoring|record for most Serie A goals in a single league match]]; during the 9–1 victory against [[F.C. Internazionale Milano|Inter Milan]] on 10 June 1961 he scored six goals; this record is jointly shared with [[Silvio Piola]] of [[U.S. Pro Vercelli Calcio|Pro Vercelli]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://storiedicalcio.altervista.org/blog/silvio_piola.html|title=PIOLA Silvio: il sesto senso del gol|publisher=Storie di Calcio|language=it|author1=Lorenzo Proverbio|date=February 2016|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref>

===Napoli===
In 1965, Sívori signed with [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]],<ref name="storiedicalcio"/> helping them to a third-place finish in the first season at the club; they also won the [[Cup of the Alps|Coppa delle Alpi]].<ref name="tuttosport"/> After two successful seasons at the club, Napoli's squad during the [[1967–68 Serie A|1967–68 season]] boasted several talents along with Sívori, such as goalkeeper [[Dino Zoff]], and fellow strike partner [[José Altafini]], and were considered one of the favourites to win the league title; the club took [[A.C. Milan]] all the way in the battle for the Serie A championship but eventually finished in second place, while Sívori was ruled out for most of the season due to a knee injury and several clashes with manager Bruno Pesaola. Ironically, Sívori's last game for Napoli was against his former club Juventus, in which he was given a [[Red card (sports)|red card]] for kicking [[Erminio Favalli]], and was suspended for six matches. Following his ban, Sívori decided to return to Argentina during the [[1968–69 Serie A|1968–69]] season.<ref name="treccani1"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://storiedicalcio.altervista.org/blog/sivori_napoli.html|title=Sivori: Fuga da Napoli|date=18 November 2015|publisher=Storie di Calcio|language=it|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref>

==International career==
===Argentina===
[[File:Sívori (Selección Argentina) - El Gráfico 1905.jpg|thumb|Sívori champion of América with Argentina in 1957]]

At international level, Sívori defended the [[Argentina national football team]] eighteen times and registered nine goals.<ref name="omar sivori">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=/news/2005/02/19/db1902.xml&sSheet=/portal/2005/02/19/ixportal.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070311102537/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=/news/2005/02/19/db1902.xml&sSheet=/portal/2005/02/19/ixportal.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 March 2007 |title="Omar Sivori". The Telegraph, 19 February 2005. Retrieved 23 October 2006 |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=30 March 1987 |location=London}}</ref> The Argentine side of the time had a formidable attack with Sívori, [[Oreste Corbatta]], [[Osvaldo Héctor Cruz|Osvaldo Cruz]], [[Humberto Maschio]] and [[Antonio Valentín Angelillo|Antonio Angelillo]]. The attacking trio of Sívori, Maschio, and Angelillo were nicknamed the ''caras sucias'', which literally means ''dirty faces'' in Spanish; in reference to the film of the same name, and due to way they played the game, like fun, dirty faced, mischievous children.<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="telegraph-sivori-obituary"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elgrafico.com.ar/2015/08/25/C-8330-enrique-omar-sivori-el-ultimo-carasucia.php|title=Enrique Omar Sívori, el último carasucia|publisher=El Gráfico|language=es|date=25 August 2015|access-date=18 June 2017}}</ref>

Sívori defended Argentina to the gold medal [[1957 South American Championship]] in [[Lima, Peru]]. Argentina dominated in every game during that year's [[Copa América|South American Championship]]; the team's wins throughout the competition included an 8–2 victory against the [[Colombia national football team]], and a 3–0 victory against close rivals [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].

===Italy===
Sívori moved to Italy in 1957, along with his compatriots Maschio and Angelillo. The Argentine football association banned the attacking trio from playing for Argentina, and eliminated them from the [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958 World Cup]].<ref name="telegraph-sivori-obituary"/> Sívori's Italian ancestry enabled him to become an Italian citizen. In April 1961 he made his debut for [[Italy national football team|Italy]].<ref name="omar sivori"/> Along with several other [[Oriundo|foreign-born Italian players]], Sívori played for Italy at the [[1962 FIFA World Cup]] in Chile, where they suffered a first-round elimination.<ref name="treccani1"/> He would earn nine caps and score eight goals while playing for Italy.<ref name="omar sivori"/>

==Playing style==
[[File:Omar Sívori in training with Juventus FC at Campo Combi.jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.13|Sívori in training during his years in Turin]]

''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'' has described Sívori's playing style as "audacious and brilliant";<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|url=http://www.britannica.com/eb/article-9403657/Sivori-Omar#853011.hook |title= Omar Sivori|encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316195951/http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/1090433/Omar-Sivori|archive-date=16 March 2014}}</ref> a highly talented footballer, he is considered one of Italy's and Juventus's greatest ever players, as well as one of the best players of his generation. Sívori was a quick, diminutive, highly creative, and technically gifted [[Forward (association football)|forward]], known for his pace on the ball, who used his acceleration, outstanding [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] skills, flair, and [[Dummy (football)|feints]] to beat opposing defenders; these included turns, flicks, quick changes of direction, and his innovative trademark move: the [[Nutmeg (football)|nutmeg]], also known as ''tunnel'', in Italian, which involved him playing the ball between an opponent's legs. He was primarily a left footed player, and was an excellent finisher and a prolific goalscorer, who possessed a powerful and accurate shot from both inside and outside the area, and who had the ability to score not only with his left, but also his right foot and, in spite of his short stature, his head; this would sometimes see him receiving kicks to the face. Despite not being particularly strong, due to his slender physique, Sívori was also known for his tenacity and bravery on the pitch, as well as his professionalism as a footballer, although he also drew criticism at times for his volatile character and unsportsman-like behaviour, which often saw him argue with officials, commit aggressive tackles on his opponents, or attempt "to provoke and to humiliate" other players with his skill on the ball.<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="telegraph-sivori-obituary"/><ref name="tuttojuve1">{{cite web|url=http://www.tuttojuve.com/gli-eroi-bianconeri/gli-eroi-in-bianconero-omar-sivori-337745|title=Gli eroi in bianconero: Omar SIVORI|publisher=Tutto Juve|language=it|author1=Stefano Bedeschi|date=2 October 2016|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="tuttosport"/><ref name="treccani1">{{cite web|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/omar-enrique-sivori_%28Enciclopedia-dello-Sport%29/|title=SIVORI, Omar Enrique|publisher=Treccani: Enciclopedia dello Sport (2002)|language=it|author1=Roberto Beccantini|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="uefa.com"/><ref name="taipeitimes"/><ref name="stampa">{{cite web|url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,4/articleid,1301_02_1990_0062_0028_189534|title=Breve il mondiale felice di Sivori, inventore del football impossibile|publisher=La Stampa|language=it|date=6 March 1990|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="treccani2">{{cite web|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/sivori/|title=Sivori|publisher=Treccani: Enciclopedie on line|language=it|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="corriere1">{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2010/aprile/12/SIVORI_ALTRI_EROI_VIZIO_DEL_co_9_100412052.shtml|title=SIVORI E ALTRI EROI, IL VIZIO DEL CALCIO|publisher=Il Corriere della Sera|page=29|language=it|author1=Stajano Corrado|date=12 April 2010|access-date=1 March 2017|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141009213803/http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2010/aprile/12/SIVORI_ALTRI_EROI_VIZIO_DEL_co_9_100412052.shtml|archive-date=9 October 2014}}</ref><ref name="guardian-obituary-sivori">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2005/feb/21/guardianobituaries.football|title=Omar Sivori|work=The Guardian|author=Brian Glanville|date=21 February 2005|access-date=2 October 2017}}</ref>{{Excessive citations inline|date=February 2026}}

Although he was an excellent goalscorer, especially while with Juventus, Sívori was also able to use his vision and passing accuracy to [[Assist (football)|create chances]] for team-mates, working in unison with [[John Charles|Charles]] and [[Giampiero Boniperti|Boniperti]] in the club's attacking trident, and was capable of playing both in the [[Forward (association football)#Centre-forward|centre]] as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|main striker]] and in a deeper role as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|second striker]] or inside forward on the [[Forward (association football)#Winger|left side of the pitch]]. Because of his creative playing style, skill, eye for goal, country of birth, hairstyle, strong mentality, and at times rebellious nature both on and off the field, Sívori is often retroactively compared to another left–footed Argentine player who emerged after him: [[Diego Maradona]], with some parts of the media dubbing him "the Maradona of the Sixties".<ref name="storiedicalcio"/><ref name="telegraph-sivori-obituary"/><ref name="tuttojuve1"/><ref name="independent-Sivori">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/omar-sivori-483923.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220524/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/omar-sivori-483923.html |archive-date=24 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Omar Sivori|work=The Independent|author=Alex Murphy|date=19 February 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://thescotsman.scotsman.com/sport.cfm?id=189042005 |title=Tributes for Sivori, an 'angel' with some heavenly moves |work=The Scotsman |date=19 February 2005}}</ref><ref>[http://www.newagebd.com/2005/feb/24/total.html Total Sports] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060513144847/http://www.newagebd.com/2005/feb/24/total.html |date=13 May 2006 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.squarefootball.net/article/article.asp?aid=945 SquareFootball.net] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071018080209/http://squarefootball.net/article/article.asp?aid=945 |date=18 October 2007 }}</ref>{{Excessive citations inline|date=February 2026}}

==Managerial career==
[[File:Sivori dt central.jpg|thumb|upright=0.81|Sívori as manager of [[Rosario Central]], 1969–70]]

Sívori retired from the playing field in 1969. Although he retired to his native Argentina as a wealthy man, his love for the game meant that he decided to take up a further career as a coach; he coached River Plate, [[Rosario Central]], [[Estudiantes de La Plata]], [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]] and [[Club Atlético Vélez Sarsfield|Vélez Sarsfield]].

From 1972 until 1974, Sívori took charge of the Argentina national team, and the team qualified for the [[1974 FIFA World Cup]]. Sívori was the first man to call up [[Ubaldo Fillol]] to defend Argentina. Fillol would become one of the most highly regarded keepers in Argentine history. After that he became a full-time [[Scout (sport)|scout]] in South America for Juventus. In 1983, he was the head coach for [[Toronto Italia]] in the [[Canadian National Soccer League|National Soccer League]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Cosgrove|first=Michael|date=29 August 1983|title=Italia takes final over Panhellenic|page=S4|work=The Globe and Mail}}</ref>

==After retirement==
In March 2004, Sívori was named by [[Pelé]] as one of the top 125 greatest living footballers and honoured as part of the [[FIFA 100]].<ref name="Pele">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3533891.stm|title=Pele's list of the greatest|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 March 2004|access-date=15 June 2013}}</ref> The following year in February 2005, Sívori died in his hometown of [[San Nicolás de los Arroyos|San Nicolás]] at the age of 69 due to [[pancreatic cancer]].<ref name="morto">{{cite web|url=http://www.corriere.it/Primo_Piano/Sport/2005/02_Febbraio/17/sivori.shtml|title=Calcio: è morto Omar Sivori|publisher=Il Corriere della Sera|language=it|date=18 February 2005|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref>

==Career statistics==

'''Individual'''
* [[Panamerican Championship]] top scorer: [[1956 Panamerican Championship|1956]] 
* [[Copa América records and statistics|South American Championship player of the tournament]]: [[1957 South American Championship|1957]]
* ''[[Capocannoniere]]'': [[1959–60 Serie A|1959–60]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/italtops.html |title=Italy – Serie A Top Scorers |author1=Roberto Di Maggio |author2=Igor Kramarsic |author3=Alberto Novello |date=11 June 2015 |access-date=2 December 2015 |url-status=live |website=[[RSSSF]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031163443/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesi/italtops.html |archive-date=31 October 2015 }}</ref>

* [[FIFA 100]]: 2004<ref name="Pele"/>
* [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics|IFFHS]] Argentina All Times Dream Team (Team B): 2021<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-all-time-argentina-mens-dream-team-9-1239|title=IFFHS ALL TIME ARGENTINA MEN'S DREAM TEAM|date=26 August 2021}}</ref>
*[[Juventus FC Hall of Fame]]: 2025<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 September 2025 |title=Juventus creates its Hall of Fame - Juventus |url=https://www.juventus.com/en/news/articles/juventus-creates-its-hall-of-fame |access-date=10 September 2025 |website=Juventus.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Filmography==
Sívori played the part of himself, in two Italian films.<ref>[https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0803417/ Sívori played the part of himself, in two Italian films] IMDb.com</ref>
*''Idoli controluce'' – (1965)
*''[[The President of Borgorosso Football Club]]'' (1970)

==Quotes==
*[[Giampiero Boniperti]]: "Playing alongside him was pure fun. Charles was the target man, while Omar used the space to put defenders in trouble. He used to play with socks down around his ankles, without any kind of protection, to show he wasn't scared of defenders. He had an incredible winning mentality."<ref name="uefa.com">[http://www.uefa.com/uefa/history/obituaries/newsid=281090.html UEFA.com] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070104214805/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/history/obituaries/newsid=281090.html |date=4 January 2007 }}</ref>
*[[John Charles]]: "With Sivori, it was the classic big man-little man partnership. Sivori had huge skill and it was a joy to play with a player as good as he was."<ref name="independent-Sivori"/>
*[[Marcello Lippi]]: "Whenever we were talking about Juventus, his eyes brightened up."<ref name="uefa.com"/>
*[[Humberto Maschio]]: "He was amazing. A first-class dribbler who had speed and the ability to surprise at any moment."<ref name="taipeitimes">{{cite web|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/sport/archives/2005/02/20/2003223911|title=Argentinian legend Enrique Omar Sivori dies at age of 69 |work=Taipei Times |date=10 April 2013}}</ref>
*[[Roberto Bettega]]: "He was like an older brother for me. He was my idol when I was a kid and then we became close friends. He was one of the best players in the history of football."<ref name="uefa.com"/>
